scene: Evening hymn, two angelic guardians, Nino Visconti, serpent repelled and Corrado Malaspina
story: As evening settles over the valley, a soul raises its hands and sings the Compline hymn Te lucis ante terminum. The others join in, attentive to the coming darkness.
Two angels with green garments and luminous wings descend from above, each bearing a blunt, flame-like sword. Sordello tells Dante they have come to guard the valley from a serpent.
Dante meets Nino Visconti, a former judge of Gallura, who is surprised to learn Dante is alive and asks that his daughter Giovanna pray for him. Nino speaks bitterly of his widow's remarriage.
Three brilliant stars shine in the evening sky, replacing the four that Dante saw at dawn. Sordello draws his attention to the change.
A serpent moves among the grass. The two angels descend swiftly and put it to flight; their defense is directly observed, without claiming to have changed the night itself.

Dante speaks with Corrado Malaspina, who asks about his family and foretells that Dante will learn their hospitality firsthand. The travelers remain within the night-bound valley, awaiting the next passage.

semanticSomatic.semantic: Nightfall turns activity toward a shared appeal for protection
Guardians can intercept a threat while travelers remain unable to climb
Remembered kinship and petitions for prayer survive death within the poem
A threat may approach a resting place without defeating its protection
Observation distinguishes changing sky, approaching danger and effective defense
A speaker can offer a future claim without converting it into a completed event

alchemicalReading: The vessel remains closed at night but protection is active inside it; the guardian function preserves the boundary until the next ascent.
invariant: A protected pause can maintain continuity and respond to threats without opening the still-closed ascent gate.
